t: Annexed by Octavian in 30 BCE, Egypt was ruled by a prefect answerable to the emperor alone.
Its grain fed Rome and Constantinople, and Alexandria was a centre of trade, science and philosophy.
Christian monasticism began in its deserts, and after 451 most Egyptians followed the church that became the Coptic Church.
dyk: Senators were forbidden to visit Egypt without the emperor's permission, and Tiberius rebuked his nephew Germanicus for touring the country in 19 CE.
ev: Octavian takes Alexandria; Antony and Cleopatra VII die
Jewish revolt destroys the Jewish community of Alexandria
The Constitutio Antoniniana makes most free Egyptians Roman citizens
Pachomius founds communal monasteries at Tabennisi
Council of Chalcedon; most Egyptian Christians reject its creed
The Sasanian Persians take Alexandria and occupy Egypt until 629
Alexandria is surrendered by treaty to the Rashidun Caliphate
